title: The smoking gun of a newborn star
caption: The Herbig–Haro objects HH 7–11 in NGC 1333, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Five small objects glow blue near the top center of this image. They are the Herbig–Haro objects HH 7 to 11, a smoking gun left by a newborn star, and they sit inside NGC 1333, a dusty, gas-rich reflection nebula.

Herbig–Haro objects form when a young star shoots out jets of ionized gas that crash into nearby clouds at high speed. These five were made by jets from the young star SVS 13, and the collisions produced five bright clumps of light in the nebula. Each of them is heading up and to the left, away from their parent star.

They will not last. Racing outward at up to 250 000 kilometers per hour, such objects fade away within a few tens of thousands of years, a short time for astronomers. HH 7 is now about 20 000 times as far from SVS 13 as Earth is from the Sun.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took this image through visible and near-infrared filters. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Part of the data is near-infrared light the eye cannot see, and these small faint clumps would be invisible without a large telescope.

explore: NGC 1333 lies about a thousand light-years from Earth. A reflection nebula shines by scattering the light of nearby stars off its dust.
alt: Five small blue glowing clumps near the top center of a dusty nebula.
